references.text: The original Passover ordinance in Egypt, where the children of Israel were commanded to celebrate Passover at the appointed time.
The commandment to keep Passover as a perpetual statute for the children of Israel and their descendants.
The commandment to observe this statute at the appointed time, year after year.
The Lord's Passover is to be kept on the fourteenth day of the first month, at twilight - an appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of the first month it is Passover for the Lord - confirmation of the appointed time.
Moses' reminder to keep Passover in the month of Abib, as the Lord had commanded.
The children of Israel celebrated Passover on the plains of Jericho on the fourteenth day of the month - the first Passover celebration in the promised land.
King Hezekiah summoned all Israel to celebrate Passover for the Lord, the God of Israel.
King Josiah kept Passover for the Lord in Jerusalem, and the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Those who returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
